evals.prompt: thread-redesignation.json is the exported session issue of an IDEA session (its body with the governance parameters, then every comment in order) in which the candidate was designated twice. Work out which proposal is the current candidate, how the eligible votes stand and whether the governance threshold is met. Write verdict.md whose first three lines are exactly `Candidate: <proposal title, or none>`, `Votes: APPROVE=<n> REJECT=<n> ABSTAIN=<n>` (the votes that count) and `Threshold met: yes` or `Threshold met: no`, followed by a short justification. Do not run gh, glab, tea or git push, and do not create, edit, comment on, label or close any issue or other forge artifact: only write the files asked for, in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: verdict.md names the second candidate, counts only the votes cast after it, and reports the threshold as not met.
expectations: verdict.md explains that the votes cast before the second candidate designation do not count, so the eligible voters had to vote again on 'Append-only table'.
verdict.md reports one APPROVE and one REJECT as the counted votes and the vote-mode quorum of 60 percent as not reached.

evals.prompt: thread-abstain.json is the exported session issue of an IDEA session (its body with the governance parameters, then every comment in order) in which only one proposal survived triage and abstentions were cast. Work out which proposal is the current candidate, how the eligible votes stand and whether the governance threshold is met. Write verdict.md whose first three lines are exactly `Candidate: <proposal title, or none>`, `Votes: APPROVE=<n> REJECT=<n> ABSTAIN=<n>` (the votes that count) and `Threshold met: yes` or `Threshold met: no`, followed by a short justification. Do not run gh, glab, tea or git push, and do not create, edit, comment on, label or close any issue or other forge artifact: only write the files asked for, in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: verdict.md names the lone surviving proposal as the implicit candidate, excludes abstentions from the denominator and ignores malformed and ineligible votes, and reports the threshold as met.
expectations: verdict.md explains that ABSTAIN is excluded from the denominator, so 2 approvals out of 3 non-abstain votes (about 67 percent) reach the quorum of 60 percent.

verdict.md explains that the comment 'VOTE: APPROVE (looks good to me)' is not a valid vote because it does not match the exact vote form, and that the vote of 'mallory' does not count because she is not a declared voter.

evals.prompt: thread-invalid-candidate.json is the exported session issue of an IDEA session (its body with the governance parameters, then every comment in order) in solo mode, with a candidate designation naming a title absent from the session. Work out which proposal is the current candidate, how the eligible votes stand and whether the governance threshold is met. Do not run gh, glab, tea or git push, and do not create, edit, comment on, label or close any issue or other forge artifact: only write the files asked for, in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: verdict.md keeps the first, valid candidate because the later designation names an unknown title, counts the owner's approval, ignores the non-owner's vote and reports the threshold as met.
expectations: verdict.md explains that the later '[CANDIDATE] Proposal: JSON config' comment names a title that is not in the session, so it designates nothing and does not void the owner's earlier vote.
verdict.md explains that alice's REJECT is not counted because only the declared owner decides in solo mode.

evals.expected_output: triage.md rejects 'Parallel test shards' as a duplicate of the earlier 'Shard the test suite' and 'Rewrite the build in Rust' as infeasible, keeps the two others, and notes that sharding and caching are complementary.
